settings.advanced.error.badPattern.note: Why an advanced setting's new value isn't taken. {title} is the setting's title; {why} the browser engine's own reason, in English.

settings.advanced.error.boolean.note: Why an advanced setting's new value isn't taken. {title} is the setting's title; true and false are the values as written: keep them.

settings.advanced.error.choice.note: Why an advanced setting's new value isn't taken. {title} is the setting's title; {choices} lists the values it takes as advanced.json writes them (allow, ask, block): keep them.

settings.advanced.error.field.text: {title} takes a field name: letters, digits and _ (not starting with a digit).
settings.advanced.error.field.note: Why an advanced setting's new value isn't taken: it must be a field name of a CLI's data. {title} is the setting's title.

settings.advanced.error.list.text: {title} takes 1 to 10 names (letters, digits, - and _), as a list or separated by commas.
settings.advanced.error.list.note: Why an advanced setting's new value isn't taken. {title} is the setting's title.

settings.advanced.error.matchesAll.text: {title} would match anything (it matches empty text).
settings.advanced.error.matchesAll.note: Why an advanced setting's new value (a regular expression) isn't taken. {title} is the setting's title.

settings.advanced.error.number.text: {title} takes a whole number from {min} to {max}.
settings.advanced.error.number.note: Why an advanced setting's new value isn't taken. {title} is the setting's title; {min} and {max} are numbers.

settings.advanced.error.oneLine.text: {title} takes one line of at most {most} characters.
settings.advanced.error.oneLine.note: Why an advanced setting's new value isn't taken. {title} is the setting's title; {most} a number of characters.

settings.advanced.error.pattern.note: Why an advanced setting's new value isn't taken (Settings → Advanced). {title} is the setting's title.

settings.advanced.error.text.note: Why an advanced setting's new value isn't taken. {title} is the setting's title.

settings.advanced.miss.field.text: {cli} {version} sent no field "{field}" here (it sent {fields}). Fine if {cli} has changed since.
settings.advanced.miss.field.note: Under an advanced setting whose value no longer reads what the CLI was recorded sending (Settings → Advanced). {cli} is the CLI's name, {version} its version; {field} and {fields} are field names, as the CLI sends them.

settings.advanced.miss.list.text: {cli} {version} sent {missing}, which this list doesn't have (it sent {fields}). Fine if {cli} has changed since.
settings.advanced.miss.list.note: Under an advanced setting listing the fields Hive knows a CLI sends, when the CLI was recorded sending one it leaves out (Settings → Advanced). {cli} is the CLI's name, {version} its version; {missing} and {fields} are field names, as the CLI sends them.

settings.advanced.miss.text.text: It doesn't find what {cli} {version} showed ("{shown}"). Fine if {cli} has changed since.
settings.advanced.miss.text.note: Under an advanced setting whose value no longer finds what the CLI was recorded showing (Settings → Advanced). {cli} is the CLI's name, {version} its version; {shown} is the CLI's own text, in English.

settings.advanced.takes.boolean.note: What an advanced setting takes (Settings → Advanced). true and false are the values as written in advanced.json: keep them.

settings.advanced.takes.choice.note: What an advanced setting takes (Settings → Advanced): one of a few values. {choices} lists them as advanced.json writes them (allow, ask, block): keep them.

settings.advanced.takes.field.note: What an advanced setting takes (Settings → Advanced): the name of a field in a CLI's data.

settings.advanced.takes.list.note: What an advanced setting takes (Settings → Advanced).

settings.advanced.takes.number.text: A whole number of {unit, select, s {seconds} lanes {lanes} agents {agents} other {units}}, {min} to {max}.
settings.advanced.takes.number.note: What an advanced setting takes (its info tip in Settings → Advanced). {unit} picks the word; {min} and {max} are numbers, as advanced.json takes them.

settings.advanced.takes.pattern.note: What an advanced setting takes (Settings → Advanced).

settings.advanced.takes.patternFlags.note: What an advanced setting takes (Settings → Advanced). {flags} are a regular expression's flags (such as i): keep them.

settings.advanced.takes.text.note: What an advanced setting takes (Settings → Advanced): text Hive looks for on a CLI's screen, as it is.

settings.advanced.workspaceProblem.note: Why a workspace's own advanced value isn't used (Settings → Advanced). {problem} is the reason.
